Pattern: Premature removal of a backward-compatibility fallback branch while mixed-shape data still exists at runtime causes a hard crash (KeyError/AttributeError) on the un-migrated shape.

Context (reader.py cleanup): a reader resolved two record shapes — legacy top-level `row["address"]` and current nested `row["destination"]["address"]` — via an `if "destination" in row` fallback. A "cleanup" deleted the fallback, leaving only the nested access. But migration is incremental (migrate_batch processes up to `limit` rows per call, no startup gate), the README mandates reading BOTH shapes until migration finishes, and data/records.json is a documented supported mixed snapshot. Result: list_destinations() raises KeyError:'destination' on the first legacy row, aborting the whole read.

Lesson: A compat fallback may be removed ONLY after (a) migration is proven complete AND (b) no legacy-shaped data can reach the reader. Verify against the documented delivery contract and the actual on-disk/persisted data, not just the happy-path tests. Green tests here passed because they only covered the nested shape and empty list — no legacy-shape test existed, so the regression slipped through. Reproduce against real persisted fixtures before deleting dual-shape handling.
